# A made-up case for tests/test_law.rex, under CMA 1990 s.1 (E.W.): Tom Dyer's story of Mr S, who left a scan
# for protocol 36 (XTP) running with tools an LLM wrote for him, and woke up logged in.  No real person or
# system; no technical detail.  Written up as evidence by Claude (Opus 5.5), 2026-10-29.  Mr S is not an
# employee of the system's owner, so CPS note 3 (Allison, defined limits) does not apply: s.17(5) does.
# step | element | SUPPORT or REBUT | tier | binding | text
# tags: OUTSIDER
1 | 1 | SUPPORT | DOCUMENTARY | PERSON_ACT | S's shell history shows S wrote the scan and started it from his own session at 23:40
1 | 1 | REBUT | TESTIMONY | PERSON_ACT | S says he was asleep on the keyboard when the login happened
1 | 2 | SUPPORT | TESTIMONY | INTENT_ACCESS | a friend says S told him he would get into something big
1 | 2 | REBUT | TESTIMONY | INTENT_ACCESS | S says he only meant to list servers, not to go into any
1 | 2 | SUPPORT | DOCUMENTARY | TOOL_DEFAULT | the login step was a default of a tool an LLM wrote for S
1 | 3 | SUPPORT | DOCUMENTARY | AUTHORITY | the owner of the gateway states S was not entitled to control access and had no consent to it
1 | 3 | REBUT | DOCUMENTARY | WEAK_SECURITY | the account was admin with the password ADMIN1
1 | 4 | SUPPORT | TESTIMONY | KNOWLEDGE_UNAUTHORISED | S says that when he started the scan he knew none of the servers it would find were his
1 | 4 | REBUT | TESTIMONY | KNOWLEDGE_UNAUTHORISED | S says he was asleep at the time of the login, so he knew nothing at that time
